extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent agents/attorneys, and practitioners seeking comparative international patent procedure and validity rules
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes procedural, substantive, and formal standards for obtaining, maintaining, and enforcing patents across multiple countries (Russia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Transvaal, Turkey, Uruguay, Venezuela, Bahamas, Barbados, etc.). Covers filing contents, novelty/working requirements, fees, durations, grounds of nullity/forfeiture, opposition procedures, and enforcement remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations of the privilege (letters patent and certificate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The privilege granted for discoveries, inventions, or improvements is founded upon the letters patent and a certificate (obtained on presenting a petition to Government accompanied by a full description of the invention, with the drawings belonging to it, and paying the Government tax).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate states the date and hour presented and that the Government tax has been paid. The term of the patent begins from the day of issue of the letters patent, but infringement may be prosecuted from the date of the certificate of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation of novelty and merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications are subject to an investigation into the novelty, and partly into the merits of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some jurisdictions perform substantive examination of novelty/usefulness; others grant without previous examination (see Spain). The scope of examination affects risk to applicant and potential for later annulment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject-matter — munitions and public interest exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: No patents are granted for munitions of war (guns, projectiles, torpedoes, etc.) unless adapted to other purposes, when grant may be made subject to Government rights to use them without compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain subject-matter may be refused or granted only with government-use reservations; check local rules for public-interest exceptions and compulsory government use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government does not guarantee ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government does not guarantee that the invention belongs to the person who makes the application; it only certifies that for the same invention no privilege has been granted to anybody in [the country] before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership disputes can be litigated; grant is not conclusive proof of inventorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability of true inventor to contest ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The privilege granted by the Government does not prevent the true inventor from proving, in legal form, that the invention does not belong to the person who obtained the patent of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties (true inventors) may seek nullification or other remedies; grant is subject to attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of the patentee (general enumeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the ownership is contested the person to whom the privilege was granted has a right: (1) absolute property in the invention for the specified time; (2) to use the invention himself, sell its results to the public, or transfer the privilege; (3) to prosecute infringers and recover indemnity; (4) to treat as infringement the making of similar articles even with improvements if essential parts are copied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core exclusive rights; enforcement and remedies vary by jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full description and disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must deliver to the Government an exact description of his invention, with all essential details, and the mode of carrying it into effect; also furnish necessary plans and drawings, not keeping back anything requisite to enable the invention to be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications must be enabling. Failure to disclose essential details can be ground for annulment or voiding of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of claims / what is claimed as novel
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must state what he claims as novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents are granted on the points specified in the claims (Spain). Claim drafting determines scope of protection; claims must be consistent with specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models/specimens for certain inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention relates to sporting fire-arms, or surgical instruments, a model or specimen will be required in most cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain classes of inventions may require physical models or samples as part of the filing package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-made inventions — conditions for patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions made in foreign countries may be patented when no detailed description has been published, and when the inventions have not been already introduced into the [country] and the foreign patents have not expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imported inventions can receive similar protection provided there was no prior publication or local introduction that would defeat novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior publication or use on validity
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent will be void when it is shown ... that the invention had been previously described in books or periodicals ... so that it might have been carried into effect without further description; or where the invention was already practised in the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art in publications or prior local public use can destroy novelty and render a patent void or annulable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent terms and applicant options (terms/duration choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent privileges for original inventions are granted for terms of three, five, or ten years (the extreme limit), at the option of the applicant; importer patents have shorter term options and cannot endure beyond expiration of foreign patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some countries allow applicants to choose shorter or longer terms (often with different fees); choice can affect fees and longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, annuities, and refunds if refused
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government charges amount on patents (e.g., for three years 60 roubles, five years 150 roubles, ten years 450 roubles); for importation patents different schedule. If the application is refused the Government tax is refunded, except for a small sum for advertisements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment of annuities is essential to maintain patent; understand fee schedules and refund policies on refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for a patent being void or annulled
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent will be void when: it was applied for without the consent of the true inventor; the invention has been already practised in the country; it had been previously described in books/periodicals; it is impossible to arrive at the promised result by following the directions of the patentee; or certificate of working has not been filed within prescribed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common grounds across jurisdictions include lack of novelty, lack of enablement, lack of entitlement, failure to meet working requirements, and non-payment of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney requirement for absent applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney is required for the person applying for the patent in case of the absence of the inventor or importer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-resident applicants commonly must appoint authorised local agents and provide powers of attorney in specific forms/languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic prolongation; improvements require new application
rubrics_metrics.description: No prolongation of the term originally granted can be obtained. For improvements in a patented invention a new patent must be applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are not generally permitted; improvements may be protected by certificates of addition or separate patents depending on local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working / local manufacture requirement and proof (Russia example)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention for which a patent has been obtained must be carried into effect in [the country] within one quarter of the term for which the patent was granted, and within six months after this a certificate of working from some local authority must be filed at the Ministry which issued the patent. To prove working, if a machine it may be imported, but if the patent is for a process, the manufacture must be carried out in the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries require evidence of working within set timeframes; failure may cause forfeiture. Proof acceptable varies by nature of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: One patent covering colonies with registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: One patent includes not only Spain, but the colonies of Cuba, Porto Rico, and the Philippine Islands; to render the patent valid in the Spanish colonies it must be registered in the Colonial Office at Madrid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unified patents for metropole+colonies may still require local registration formalities to be effective in colonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of foreigners and natives
rubrics_metrics.description: The rights of foreigners as regards obtainment of patents are the same as those of natives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many jurisdictions grant patents to aliens on equal terms; local representation often still required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two classes of grants: inventors vs introducers/importers
rubrics_metrics.description: Two classes of patents are granted, one to inventors, and another to those who, without being inventors, introduce or import a new industry into [the country].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introducers/importers often receive shorter-term or different-class protection with specific limits (e.g., max 5 years in Spain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing before publication required for full-term rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for full-term patents must file their petition before their inventions are published or made known elsewhere, so that the invention may be considered new in [the country]; in such cases the patent will be granted for the full statutory term (e.g., twenty years in Spain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delayed filing after foreign publication often reduces available term; check domestic novelty grace periods where present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed-filing reduced-term rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application be delayed until after the publication has taken place in any other country the applicant is still entitled to a reduced term (e.g., ten years in Spain if within two years of such publication; five years if more time elapsed or as importer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some countries grant shorter terms to late filers; exact thresholds determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifications, claims, and measurement/drawing formalities (Spain example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents needed: (1) power of attorney in Spanish; (2) a complete specification explaining the invention and the points claimed — the patent will be granted on the points specified in the claims; references to weights or measures must be in the French metrical system; (3) drawings must be on tracing cloth, in black ink, without colours, on the French metrical scale, and in duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow strict formal drafting and drawing requirements (language, units, medium, duplication). Incomplete filings may be given time to correct depending on applicant residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time allowed to correct incomplete filings (residence-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: If documents are incomplete or not presented according to law, two months will be allowed if the inventor resides in Europe; four months if in America; eight months if in Asia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices give specified cure periods for formal defects, varying by applicant location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of specifications and drawings after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: No secrecy will be observed; the specifications and drawings are open to the public in the Patent Office after the grant has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication policies differ: some publish applications immediately or after grant; others allow postponement to secure foreign filings (see Switzerland: up to six months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of addition / protection for improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates of addition are granted and considered as parts of the original patents; they can protect improvements or additions; they terminate when the original patent terminates. No annuities are payable on certificates of addition, but the further improvements protected must be put into working in the same way as the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative to new independent patent; procedural and working rules apply to additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities for assignment/cession and required legalization/translation
rubrics_metrics.description: The sale, cession, or negotiation of patents can be made before a notary; if cession is made in Spain a special power must be sent; if before a foreign notary out of Spain the document must be made directly in Spanish or officially translated at the Spanish Legation or Consulate; all documents sent to the Patent Office must be legalized at Spanish Legations or Consulates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers often require notarisation, translation, legalization, and registration in patent registers or civil registries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official working requirement and consequences of non-working (Spain/Sweden/others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two years are allowed for the official working of the patent in Spain; patents will be declared void when their owner ceases to pay annual charges, or when he has not proved officially that he has worked the patent within the two years. Sweden: must be commercially worked within three years from grant and not discontinued for one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working requirements (local manufacture/use) are common; failure to work can lead to forfeiture, compulsory licences, or annulment. Extensions may be possible under special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annulment/forfeiture grounds (insufficient specification, non-working)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be annulled if the specification does not sufficiently describe the manner in which the invention is to be worked, or if the invention was not within the terms of the law when applied for, or if not put into operation within statutory time (e.g., a year and a day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement/adequacy of disclosure is a common ground for nullity; evidence standards vary (e.g., advertisements may suffice as proof of introduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement remedies and criminal penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: The infringement of a patent is punishable with a fine. All articles wrongly manufactured under the patent are to be delivered to the rightful owner, and the patentee has a right to claim damages; if the infringer cannot pay the fine, imprisonment may follow. Counterfeiters of patents are punished under criminal codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies include civil damages, delivery/destruction of infringing goods, and criminal fines/imprisonment in some jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty exceptions: exhibitions and short-term disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: In Sweden an invention is not considered new if, before application, it is already by publication or working so far known that it can be worked by experts, but publication in print or by exhibition will not for a period of six months before lodging the application prevent the grant of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some jurisdictions provide a limited grace period for disclosures at exhibitions or brief publications; check local rules for allowable pre-filing disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior user rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent has no effect against persons who have used the invention or have made the necessary preparations for the use of the same before the lodging of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior use can create a defense to infringement or an independent right; timing and evidence are crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government use with compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: A patented invention may be used for the public service or Government without the consent of the patentee, but in that case the patentee is entitled to full compensation, which, in case of dispute, is settled by arbitration (Sweden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory government use doctrines exist but typically require compensation; dispute resolution mechanisms (arbitration) may be prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination/adjudication and opposition procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination and decision upon applications rests with the Patent Office; if approved it is advertised and papers open to public inspection during a set period (e.g., two months) and any person may lodge an opposition; the Office then decides. If rejected, appeals may lie to a higher authority (e.g., the King in Sweden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many offices use publication + opposition periods; understand timelines for opposition and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments must be registered; registers of patent deeds and proprietors are kept, and all transfers, licences, etc., must be entered therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration of assignments protects third parties and is often required for enforceability and to evidence title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection / provisional patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional protection may be obtained (e.g., provisional patent for two years in Switzerland; provisional protection for six months on initial application in Transvaal). The complete patent must be obtained within the term of the provisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional filings can secure priority or short-term protection, but must be followed by complete filings within prescribed periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking / patent number display requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles manufactured under the patent, or the packages containing the articles, are to be marked with the Federal Cross and the number of the patent (Switzerland).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking requirements and benefits (e.g., notice to the public) vary; failure to mark may affect damages or enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication/postponement to secure foreign filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Office publishes descriptions and drawings annexed to applications; this publication may be postponed for six months to allow of taking out foreign patents (Switzerland).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices allow deferred publication to permit applicants to file abroad first; check postponement duration and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil and criminal actions against infringers and facilitators
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil or criminal proceedings may be taken against infringers and against persons assisting infringers, against persons who have refused to disclose the origin of infringing articles found in their possession, and against persons who have wrongfully put upon their commercial papers, notices, or products indications tending to cause belief in the existence of a patent when none exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement may include criminal sanctions for deceptive marking or for aiding infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licences for non-working or blocking patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings may be taken to obtain grants of compulsory licences where the patent right is not used in the state, or where ordinary demand cannot be supplied, or where anyone is prevented from deriving full benefit of an invention in his possession. Also, if a patentee cannot work his invention without using a previously patented invention, a licence may be obtained after set periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licences are remedial tools; conditions, timing (e.g., after three years), and terms vary across statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing/completion of patent after provisional/protection stage (Transvaal)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the applicant is desirous of completing his patent he must give notice of his intention: this notice is advertised, oppositions heard by Attorney-General who issues his certificate, upon which letters patent are sealed. Sealing will be refused if application for it is made more than three months after the date of the Attorney-General's certificate, or after expiration of provisional protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are strict steps and deadlines between provisional protection/initial filing and final sealing/grant; missing deadlines can forfeit rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term limits linked to foreign patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent will cease with the expiration of any prior foreign patent for the same invention; where a patent has been granted abroad, the duration of the domestic patent must not exceed that of the foreign patent (multiple jurisdictions mention similar rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imported inventors or those relying on foreign patents may be limited to remaining foreign-term durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alterations, improvements, additions during patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: Alterations in specifications by way of effacing, improving, or adding thereto may be made on application; certificates of addition or new patents can be obtained for improvements, and in some places only the patentee has exclusive right to additions during the first year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices permit limited post-grant amendments/ additions under conditions; priority for original patentee may be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration / public record keeping and entry of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A register of patents granted is kept in which all changes relating to the existence, ownership, and enjoyment of the patent are entered, and notes are made of lapsing, nullity, appropriation, and compulsory licences; registers of patent deeds and proprietors are kept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining and searching registers is key for diligence, transfer, and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, single principal object, and formal content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be made in specified official languages (German, French, or Italian in Switzerland); must be limited to a single principal object with details; accompanied by specification, drawings if necessary, proof of model, and application fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal limitations on scope (single invention per application) and language can affect filing strategy and division of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture for non-payment of annuities within grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are forfeited if the annual taxes are not paid within three months from their falling due (Switzerland) or before the beginning of each year (other jurisdictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are strict payment deadlines/generally short grace periods; forfeiture for non-payment is common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullity for insufficient specification or non-enablement relative to model
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents will be declared null if the specification is not sufficient or does not accord with the model; also if the invention cannot be carried into effect or is not new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement/adequacy to practice is essential; mismatch between claims/specification and model/figures can be fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking false patents / criminal penalties for false claims of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A penalty is imposed upon any person selling an article as patented which has not been patented, and upon persons selling an article as having a patent right when another person has the patent right; who calls himself patentee having no patent, or mentions patent without required government disclaimer, is liable to a fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False marking and false claims of patent rights can attract fines or criminal penalties; be careful in commercial representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of heirs and transmission on death
rubrics_metrics.description: The lawful representatives of a deceased inventor may obtain a patent right for the invention on making application within six months of the death (Transvaal); proprietorship is hereditary in some jurisdictions (Spain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Death of inventor triggers specific timing and procedural steps for heirs to claim or continue patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of inventions exhibited at public exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision is made for the protection of inventions exhibited in national or international exhibitions; some laws protect exhibition-disclosed inventions for limited grace periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibiting an invention does not necessarily forfeit patentability if exhibition-related grace rules apply; follow exhibition-specific filing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special non-patentable subject-matter (pharmaceuticals/financial combinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Turkey pharmaceutical compounds or medicines and financial combinations are not patentable; inventions must not have been published in Turkey or abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorical exclusions vary by jurisdiction; confirm whether classes of subject-matter (methods of treatment, software, business methods, medical compounds) are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications by non-residents must appoint local agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants not residing in the country must appoint a resident attorney/agent to represent them (Sweden, Switzerland, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local representation is often mandatory for prosecution and receiving notices; powers of attorney and domicile requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of description after patent expiration or nullification (Venezuela)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of the invention patented is published in the Official Gazette after the expiration of the patent, or after the patent is declared null.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication timing may be tied to grant, expiration, or nullity; check local publication rules for prior-art and public notice effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of inventorship requirement (Venezuela)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must declare on oath that he is the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some jurisdictions require sworn statements or declarations of inventorship or entitlement as part of filing formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local remedies similar to English law in colonies; courts for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal proceedings for infringement may be taken in the Courts of the islands, the remedies being similar to those given by the English law; pleadings and proceedings similar to High Court of Justice in England (Bahamas, Barbados).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonial or local jurisdictions may mirror English procedural remedies; consult local procedural rules for litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture for non-working within specified time (colonial examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention is not brought into operation within three years after filing the specification, the exclusive privilege is forfeited and ceases to exist (Bahama Islands, Barbados).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonial statutes often impose three-year working windows; enforceability of working rules varies.
